description: Measures the proved Milnor deficit D_A at the proton q₀ (A=3..8) against the empirical binding fraction trend, to test whether D_A is the binding magnitude. Finds OPPOSITE A-dependence (|D_A| falls geometrically + sign alternates; B/A rises via coordination), so D_A is the Milnor order/parity structure, not the magnitude — substantiating the milnor-brunnian-deficit coordination-ledger claim. No fit, no wiring; scope-(a). mpmath dps=50, zero float64.

results.verdict: MEASURED: D_A is the Milnor STRUCTURE, not the binding magnitude. At the proton q₀, |D_A| falls geometrically (ratio per step = −h²(h²+2) = -0.08932265, |·|<1) and its sign alternates as (−1)^{A−3} — the deficit is a rapidly-decaying, sign-carrying order marker. The empirical binding fraction B/A/m_N RISES with A over the light range (0.767→0.954·ℏ_q², ⁴He→⁵⁶Fe) via the coordination count z=A−1 (qou-brng, binding=−log I). The two objects have OPPOSITE A-dependence, so D_A cannot be the binding magnitude; it carries the Milnor order/parity. This substantiates with numbers the coordination-ledger claim that a MeV binding number from D_A would be a fit (the magnitude lives in the qou-brng coordination free energy, not in D_A).
